etymologies.etymologyHTML:
The noun is derived from Late Middle English somet, somete (“head, top”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman sumet and Middle French sommet (masculine), somete, sommette (“top of a thing; highest point of a mountain”) (feminine) (modern French sommet), from Old French somet, sommette, from som, sum (“highest point, summit”) + -et (suffix forming diminutive masculine nouns), -ete, -ette (suffix forming diminutive feminine nouns). Som, sum are derived from Latin summum (“top, summit”), a noun use of the neuter of summus (“greatest, highest; top, uppermost”, adjective) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *upó (“below, under”) + *-m̥mós, *-tm̥mós (“suffix forming superlative adjectives”)). The modern English spelling was influenced by summity (“height or top of a thing; utmost degree, perfection”) (obsolete).

The verb is derived from the noun.

definitions.definition: The highest point of a hill, mountain, or similar geographical feature.

quote.citation: 2021 September 17, “The Summit”, in Eternal Blue, performed by Spiritbox, Portland, Or.: Rise Records, →OCLC:
quote.text: How can I crawl up to reach those heights / And run? / The venom is what keeps me alive / The venom is what keeps me alive / Up to the summit at night / Desperate to find that beating heart of mine that always makes me run

definitions.definition: (mathematics) A vertex of a polygon or polyhedron.
(nautical, rail transport, road transport) The highest point of a canal, railway, road, etc.
(botany) Synonym of anther (“the pollen-bearing part of the stamen of a flower”); also (rare), synonym of stigma (“the sticky part of a flower that receives pollen during pollination”)

(crystallography, rare) One of the two vertices of a crystal with a rhombohedral shape where the angles of each face are equal; also, the highest point of a crystal with a pyramidal or tetrahedral shape.
The topmost point or surface of a thing; the apex, the peak.
The highest point of achievement, development, etc., that can be reached; the acme, the pinnacle.
(archaic) The highest level of political leadership.
(by extension) An assembly or gathering of the leaders of countries to discuss issues of international significance; also (loosely), an important or high-level gathering or meeting.
(transitive, climbing, informal) To reach the summit (noun sense 1.1) of (a mountain).

quote.citation: 2012 July–August, Kenza Moller, “Eyes on the North”, in Canadian Geographic, volume 132, number 4, Ottawa: Royal Canadian Geographical Society, →ISSN, →OCLC, page 10:
quote.text: Of the range's 12 peaks, Mount Saskatchewan is the only one that has yet to be summited.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, climbing, informal) To reach the summit of a mountain.
(intransitive, politics) To attend a summit (noun sense 2.2.2).

quote.citation: 1969, Economic and Political Weekly, volume 4, numbers 14-26, page 645:
quote.text: If the Soviet leaders could go on summiting with the US while bombs poured on North Vietnam and yet claim that they had nothing but the best interests of the Vietnamese revolution in mind, there seems precious little reason to cry wolf at Peking-Bonn relations.
[…]  what the North Vietnamese would do while Richard Nixon was summiting in Moscow.  […]

quote.citation: 1998, David S. Nuttall, Mickey Mantle's Greatest Hits, page 152:
quote.text: The young President [JFK], who is on the eve of summiting with Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev, is ensconced at Hyannis Port, Massachusetts, preparing to fly to Vienna with his wife, Mrs. Jacqueline Kennedy, to meet with Khrushchev to discuss Cold War issues.

quote.citation: 2001, Robert V. Heffernan, Cabinetmakers: Story of the Three-year Battle to Establish the U.S. Department of Education, page 439:
quote.text: The President had been summiting with Soviet President Leonid Brezhnev in Vienna.

quote.citation: 2021, Mark LaVoie, Reagan’s Soviet Rhetoric: Telling the Soviet Redemption Story, page 92:
quote.text: From May 29 to June 3, 1988[,] Reagan and Gorbachev summited in Moscow. Expectations of the meeting were low, because Reagan's position as a "lame duck" president guaranteed that nothing new of historic import would occur.

definitions.definition: (England, especially Lancashire, Yorkshire, informal) Alternative spelling of summat (“something”)
